serializedLocalizedConversation.mainText:
You: {f_botName}, do you know about home pets?
Bot: …
Bot: Yes, I just checked what that phrase means. They are small animals that are kept in people’s houses.
You: Would you want to have one?
Bot: Why? Aren’t they just eating food and sleeping? 
You: W-well, for the most part you are right, but they are also used for many helpful tasks. For example dogs can be used for home protection, hunting or as a guide dog.
Bot: I assure you, I’m far more suited for home defence than some mutt.
Mutt?! Where did she learn this word…
Bot: We do not hunt. Nor do we need a guiding dog.
You: Aren’t they cute and stuff? Everyone loves pets for their fluffy furrs and the affection they offer.
Bot: That’s just a marketing strategy that is deeply rooted in human culture and also in pets’ genetics as well.
You: Genetics?! Come on, that’s exaggerating. 
Bot: Just think about it. For example, humans were selectively breeding dogs for thousands of years to develop the characteristics that would be the most useful and sell best. 
Bot: Dogs are called man's best friend? Man’s best tool or man’s best product would suit better.
You: That’s harsh… 
You: I love dogs and cats, they are great! Have you watched some of these funny videos on the internet? I’m sure you wouldn’t be so sceptical about them if you did.
Bot: I’m aware of them. What’s up with this whole conversation? It sounds like you are the one who wants to have a pet.
You: M-maybe? I had a dog when I was younger, it was a lot of work to take care of it, but I do not regret it.
Bot: Why now of all times?
You: Just a random thought, nothing much.
Bot: If it is the affection you are after…
#bot.Expression.Blush
Bot: Aren’t I enough?
Damn…
When she’s saying things like that, I can’t really find any counter arguments.
I guess we don’t need any pets for now…
